paper.title: Bandit Learning to Rank with Position-Based Click Models: Personalized and Equal Treatments

settings.name_in_paper: MAB-based ONL2R with position-based click model, personalized treatment
unmapped: Position-based click model: user type i observes exactly one of the m ranked positions with unknown probability rho_{i,k}, then clicks the arm there with unknown probability mu_{i,j}; learner observes a click/no-click reward (and which arm was clicked), but not which position was observed when there is no click
User types (M_ctx = N in the paper) arrive i.i.d. with unknown rates lambda_i and are observed before ranking
Paper's M arms map to K, paper's K positions map to m
UCBRank's tuning a_t > 2/min mu_{i,j} requires knowledge of a lower bound on the minimum arm mean
settings.definition_quote: consider a stochastic bandit setting with a set of user types $[N]$, a set of arms $[M]$, and a set of ranking positions $[K]$, where $K\leq M$. ... user $I(t)$ randomly observes an arm $J(t)$ at ranked position $\sigma_t(J(t))$ with probability $\rho_{I(t),\sigma_t(J(t))}$, and then clicks arm $J(t)$ with probability $\mu_{I(t), J(t)}$. The learner receives a reward $r(t) = 1$ if some position is clicked ... Personalized Treatment: ... an optimal policy always recommends the optimal permutation denoted by $\sigma_i^*$ regarding the arrived user type $i$

settings.name_in_paper: MAB-based ONL2R with position-based click model, equal treatment (collective utility function)
unmapped: Position-based click model with unknown position preferences rho_{i,k} and click rates mu_{i,j}; position not revealed without a click

Objective is a collective utility Gamma(sigma) = sum_i lambda_i f(sum_j rho_{i,sigma(j)} mu_{i,j}) with a known utility function f (utilitarian, Nash, ...); the same ranking must be shown to all user types
Learner knows the utility function f (and uses L_f in tuning a_t) and a lower bound on min mu_{i,j}
Paper's M arms map to K, paper's K positions map to m, paper's N user types map to M_ctx
settings.definition_quote: Equal treatment: ... an equal treatment ranking policy makes an identical ranking decision among all user groups ... $\Gamma(\sigma) \triangleq \sum_{i\in[N]} \lambda_i \cdot f(\sum_{j\in \mathrm{M}_{\sigma}} \rho_{i,\sigma(j)}\cdot \mu_{i,j})$ ... $\mathbb{E}[R(t)] = t\cdot\Gamma(\sigma^*) - \sum_{s=1}^t \mathbb{E}[\Gamma(\sigma_s)]$.

symbols.sum_types: sum over user types i in [N]
symbols.lambda_i: arrival rate of user type i
symbols.mu_min_i: min_j mu_{i,j} for user type i

source.label: thm_greedy1
source.quote: Setting $\varepsilon_t=t^{-1/2}$, the expected regret of GreedyRank Option 1 at any time step $t$ can be bounded as follows: $\mathbb{E}[R(t)]\leq 2N\sqrt{t} + \sum_{i\in[N]}\cfrac{8C_\rho MK\sqrt{\lambda_it}\ln t}{(1-1/C)\min_j\mu_{i,j}} + \mathcal{O}(1)$, where $C, C_\rho >1$ are problem-dependent constants.

results.notes: Exact bound plus O(1) recorded with O notation. Paper's M arms -> K, K positions -> m, N types -> M_ctx. The proof sets epsilon_t = N t^{-1/2}, inconsistent with statement. Regret is against per-user-type optimal ranking, defined via means.

symbols.sum_types: sum over user types i in [N]
symbols.lambda_i: arrival rate of user type i
symbols.Delta_min_i: min_j Delta_{i,j}, minimum gap for user type i

source.label: thm_ucb1
source.quote: Setting $a_t\in(2/\min\mu_{i,j}, \sqrt{t/\ln t}]$, the expected regret of UCBRank Option 1 at any time step $t$ can be bounded as follows: $\mathbb{E}[R(t)] \leq \sum_{i\in[N]}\cfrac{2C_\rho MK\sqrt{\lambda_i t\ln t}}{\min_j\Delta_{i,j}} + \mathcal{O}(1)$.

results.notes: Delta_{i,j} not formally defined in the paper. Tuning requires a lower bound on min mean.

symbols.delta_s: approximation error of the argmax solver at round s

source.label: thm_greedy2
source.quote: Setting $\varepsilon_t=N t^{-1/2}$, with a $\delta_t$-approximate solution to the maximization problem in GreedyRank Option 2, the expected regret of Fair-GreedyRank at any time step $t$ can be bounded by: $\mathbb{E}[R(t)]\leq 2Nt^{1\over 2} + \cfrac{8L_fC_\rho NMK}{(1-1/C)\min\mu_{i,j}}t^{1\over 2}\ln t + \sum_{s=1}^t f(1)N\delta_s + \mathcal{O}(1)$

results.notes: Per-round argmax over permutations may be NP-hard; compute not stated.

source.label: thm_greedy2
source.quote: and for $\delta_t=\mathcal{O}(t^{-1})$, we have: $\mathbb{E}[R(t)] = \mathcal{O}\left( 8L_f NMKt^{1\over 2}\log t/ \min\mu_{i,j} \right)$.

results.notes: Second part of the same theorem.

symbols.Delta_Gamma: Gamma(sigma*) minus the CUF of the best suboptimal permutation

tuning: delta_t = O(sqrt(log t / t)) approximation accuracy

source.label: thm_ucb2
source.quote: With any $\delta_t$-approximate solution to the maximization problem in UCBRank Option 2, setting $\delta=\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\log t/t})$ and $a_t\in(2L_f/\min\mu_{i,j}, \sqrt{t/\ln t}]$, the expected regret of UCBRank at any time step $t$ can be bounded as follows: $\mathbb{E}[R(t)] = \mathcal{O}\left( \cfrac{N^2MK\sqrt{t\log t}}{\Delta_{\Gamma}} \right)$.

results.notes: Proof's final bound also contains a C_1 f(1) N ln t term.
